preamble: Fronting of the velar stop [k] to the palatal stop [c] before front vowels or [j] is one of the most common coarticulatory changes. It is allophonic in Modern Greek, Turkish and Icelandic, where the palatal realization stays a stop rather than proceeding to an affricate, and it is the usual first stage of velar palatalization chains that end in [tʃ] or [ts].

examples.note: The velars /k, ɡ, x, ɣ/ have palatal allophones [c, ɟ, ç, ʝ] before the front vowels /e, i/.
In native words /k, ɡ/ are realized as [c, ɟ] next to the front vowels /e, i, œ, y/; in loanwords the palatal is contrastive (kar 'snow' vs kâr [car] 'profit').
Velar stops become palatal before /ɛ ei ɪ i/ and /j/; compare kjóla [ˈcʰouːla] 'dresses' with kóla [ˈkʰouːla] 'cola'.
